scores.evidence: Both term tables (worktree / background execution, unattended run / scheduled task) stack cleanly at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-03.png, pages/mobile-jp-12.png and pages/mobile-jp-13.png). The two code blocks highlight the important lines 13/17 and 2, 12-16, and fit without horizontal scroll (pages/mobile-jp-06.png, pages/mobile-jp-20.png). The lesson has no diagram, though, so how worktrees, branches and the merge relate is told in words and code only.

metrics.json reports textOnlyScreens empty on both devices. Desktop charsPerLine median is 37, inside the JP 30-40 target. Every mobile screen breaks prose with a table, code, steps, a callout or a check, and the full-length rhythm shows no wall of text or empty gap.

The lesson is Japanese only, and every visible label, button and diagram-free figure is in Japanese with English glosses on first use, for example 'ワークツリー（worktree）'. Inline code chips stay whole and readable at 390 px, for example the option chips in the exam (pages/mobile-jp-25.png). Contrast is good, and nothing is hidden under the top or bottom bars.

niceToHave: Add a small flowchart TD to the worked-example section (3 nodes or so: 本体 -> .claude/worktrees/feature-a and bugfix-b -> git merge) so learners see how the two worktrees and branches relate. Today the relationship is only in the code block and steps (pages/mobile-jp-05.png, pages/mobile-jp-06.png).

The flag names in the practice-1 checklist ('--bare を付けています', '--permission-mode dontAsk で…') show as bold proportional text, not code chips, unlike the rest of the lesson (pages/mobile-jp-19.png, pages/desktop-jp-13.png). Wrap them in backticks for consistency, if the checklist block supports inline code.

In the model-answer code block, the prompt string (lines 3-11) sits flush left while the flags are indented, so the quoted string is a little harder to tell apart from the command (pages/mobile-jp-20.png). Indenting the string lines by two spaces would make the structure clearer.
Desktop charsPerLine max is 51, above the 30-40 target. The median is 37, so this is advisory only.

summary: metrics.json shows no hard failures: no overflow and no console, mermaid, block or image errors. The lessonHash is copied from metrics.json. No personal data appears on any of the screens I opened. Tables, highlighted code, steps and checks render cleanly on all 31 mobile and 21 desktop screens, with nothing cut off at 390 px. The most useful optional improvement is a small diagram of the worktree, branch and merge flow.
